grid_kgco2e_per_kwh.source: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector v17.0, weighted average, FY2020-21 (CO2 only). Replace with the latest CEA version.

gwp_ch4.source: IPCC AR5 100-year GWP for methane. AR6 gives 27.0 (non-fossil) and 29.8 (fossil); use the report your target registry requires.

landfill_kgco2e_per_kg_organic.source: MoEFCC / NITI Aayog national waste sector modeling assumptions for deep unmanaged Indian dumpsites: High-decomposition DOCf 0.77 (due to approximately 35Â°C average landfill temperature), DOC 0.15, MCF 0.8, F 0.5, multiplied by 16/12 and GWP 28. Assumes 0% gas recovery and 0% surface oxidation.

truck_kgco2e_per_tkm.source: UK Defra/BEIS conversion factors 2025, rigid diesel HGV average laden, 0.19748, via Climatiq. UK vehicles; India values differ.

gwp_n2o.source: IPCC AR5 100-year GWP for nitrous oxide. Kept on AR5 for consistency with gwp_ch4; AR6 gives 273.

composting_ch4_kg_per_t_wet.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 5 Ch. 4, Table 4.1, composting default CH4 emission factor (wet weight basis).

composting_n2o_kg_per_t_wet.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 5 Ch. 4, Table 4.1, composting default N2O emission factor (wet weight basis).

stationary_combustion_ch4_kg_per_kwh.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2 Ch. 2, Table 2.2, 'other primary solid/gaseous biomass' default 1 kg CH4/TJ (= 3.6e-6 kg/kWh). Applied to combusted syngas and pyrolysis oil/gas.

stationary_combustion_n2o_kg_per_kwh.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2 Ch. 2, Table 2.2, biomass gases default 0.1 kg N2O/TJ (= 3.6e-7 kg/kWh).

fossil_heat_kgco2_per_kwh.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2 Ch. 1, Table 1.4, residual fuel oil 77,400 kg CO2/TJ. The value is sourced; the ASSUMPTION is that pyrolysis oil/gas displaces industrial furnace oil 1:1 on an energy basis. Confirm the offtaker's actual displaced fuel.

biochar_carbon_fraction.source: IPCC 2019 Refinement, Vol. 4 Ch. 2, Appendix 4, Table 4A.1 organic-carbon fraction for herbaceous-feedstock pyrolysis biochar, used as a proxy for mixed organic waste. Requires lab ultimate analysis of the actual char.

biochar_permanence_fraction.unit: fraction of biochar C remaining after 100 years
biochar_permanence_fraction.source: IPCC 2019 Refinement, Vol. 4 Ch. 2, Appendix 4, Table 4A.2 F_perm for medium-temperature (450-600 C) pyrolysis biochar. Only valid if the char is applied to soil, not burned.

organic_lhv_dry_mj_per_kg.source: Typical lower heating value of dry food/garden waste used to size syngas energy in the gasification branch. Replace with bomb-calorimeter data for the actual feedstock.
